children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE Futures canola contracts were sharply lower at midday Friday, as traders took profits ahead of the United States Department of Agriculture's monthly supply/demand estimates.
- November canola was down by C$15.50 at C$823.80 per tonne at midsession.
- Chart-based positioning was a feature, with canola at its lowest levels of the past week.

- Any surprises in the USDA yield and production data, set for release at 12:00 EDT, could sway the futures ahead of the close. While pre-report trade estimates are mixed, average trade guesses call for small cuts to U.S. soybean yields and production.
- Forecasts calling for the chance of frost in northern reaches of the Canadian Prairies over the weekend were supportive.
- An estimated 33,300 canola contracts traded as of 11:21 EDT.
